method: Registry data came from RIPE DB REST (aut-num and organisation objects, with unfiltered), ARIN Whois-RWS and RDAP (rdap.arin.net, which redirects to APNIC, LACNIC and AFRINIC), APNIC RDAP entity search plus a whois query on whois.apnic.net for ASNs by organisation, AFRINIC and LACNIC RDAP, and ARIN org-to-ASN lookups. PeeringDB name search (4 s pauses) and public operator home pages (title, description and visible text only, no sign-in) were used to classify what each network does. rdap.org was rate-limited (HTTP 1015) and not used. Where RIPE holds a RIPE-NONAUTH copy of an ARIN or APNIC number (AS22351, AS9229, AS37572), the authoritative RIR record is used where one exists. RIPE 'created' values of 1970-01-01 are placeholders and recorded as null. ARIN RDAP gives no country on autnum objects, so the holder organisation's country is used. Coverage limit: name searches only, so ASNs held under unrelated or unexpected names are missed, and the RIPE and APNIC searches are far more complete than ARIN's, LACNIC's, AFRINIC's or JPNIC/KRNIC's. Several operator sites (Iridium, Kacific, Thuraya, Arabsat, Space42, Gilat) blocked automated fetches, so those rows are 'registry only'. Unrelated name hits (Hughes Hubbard & Reed AS27378 and AS33520, Hughes Brothers AS19728, Verizon's Hughes Telematics AS46639) were checked and left out. Carried traffic was not measured; classes rest on holder names and operator websites. Five rows (AS27277, AS49854, AS50494, AS204791, AS218203) were rechecked on 20 Nov 2026 against routing data from RIPEstat (announced prefixes, routing history, neighbours, abuse contacts) and, where a domain was found, the holder's home page.
